claims.text: The Bank of Korea's Monetary Policy Decision & Opening Remarks to the Press Conference (16 July 2026) states: "Stock prices underwent a sizable correction amid heightened volatility due to growing concerns over AI investment and large-scale net sales of domestic stocks by foreign investors," and that "financial stability risks also persist," including elevated exchange-rate volatility.

Re-checked 12 August 2026: the Ministry of Economy and Finance's English press-center page shows no crisis-specific statement newer than the 29 July 2026 Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting readout; the next newer item in its listing is a routine piece on the US Treasury's semiannual FX-policy report. The Bank of Korea's English homepage rendered successfully today (unlike recent placeholder failures); its most recent items are routine releases -- May 2026 balance-of-payments data (6 August), North Korea 2025 GDP estimates (31 July), Q2 2026 GDP advance estimate (23 July), and the 16 July rate decision (2.50% to 2.75%) -- none addressing stock-market volatility or new stabilization measures.

Re-checked 13 August 2026: MOFE's press-center list and the Bank of Korea's press-release list show no new crisis-specific release since the 29 July 2026 Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting; BOK's English press-release page remains in a maintenance placeholder state. No IMF statement on the correction has been published. No allowlisted source has declared the episode resolved.

Re-checked 14 August 2026: MOFE's press-center list and the Bank of Korea's press-release page (still a maintenance placeholder) show no crisis-specific release newer than the 29 July 2026 Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting; no allowlisted source has declared the episode resolved.

Neither the Bank of Korea nor the Ministry of Economy and Finance has issued a new crisis-level statement since the 29 July 2026 Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting; MOFE's English press-release list shows no stock-market-stabilization item between 30 July and 12 August 2026, and BOK's most recent monetary policy decision remains 16 July 2026 (rate raised 2.50% to 2.75%), with no newer policy statement found as of this check.

South Korea's Ministry of Economy and Finance's press release "Authorities Step Up Swift Coordination and Response Amid Heightened Stock Market Volatility" (29 July 2026) states the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance and Economy convened an Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting attended by the Bank of Korea Governor and the Chairmen of the Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service, after "the recent sharp decline in the stock market, led by semiconductor shares, was driven by intensifying competition in the memory chip industry stemming from China and growing concerns over funding needs among major U.S. technology companies"; the authorities announced investor-specific investment limits on single-stock leveraged products, higher transaction costs, mandatory simulated trading, and a commitment to establish a legal basis for emergency market-stabilization measures.

Re-checked 5 August 2026: the Ministry of Economy and Finance's Press Releases list, sorted newest-first, shows 'Consumer Price Index, July 2026' (August 4, 2026), 'Monthly Industrial Statistics, June 2026' (July 31, 2026), and 'Treasury Bond Issuance Plan, August 2026' (July 30, 2026) as the entries posted after the 'Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting' release (July 29, 2026); none of these newer entries concerns stock-market volatility or intervention, so the 29 July emergency-meeting readout remains the latest official statement on the market correction.

Re-confirmed by direct fetch on 6 August 2026: the Ministry of Economy and Finance's press release list shows no statement newer than 29 July 2026 (Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting) addressing stock-market volatility or intervention; the most recent entries since (30 July Treasury Bond Issuance Plan, 31 July Monthly Industrial Statistics, 4 August Consumer Price Index) are routine releases unrelated to the correction.

Re-checked 7 August 2026: the Bank of Korea's press-release listing and the Ministry of Economy and Finance's English-language site did not expose a statement list via direct fetch this session (client-rendered / temporarily unavailable); no non-allowlisted reporting found a new BOK or Ministry of Economy and Finance statement addressing the stock-market situation since the 29 July 2026 Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting readout.

Re-checked 8 August 2026: the Ministry of Economy and Finance's press-release list still shows the 29 July 2026 'Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting' as the latest release addressing the market correction (subsequent releases, e.g. the 2026 Tax Revision Bill and July CPI, are routine and unrelated); the Bank of Korea's press-release page remained unrenderable today, and no newer market-stabilization statement was confirmed from either allowlisted source.

Re-checked 9 August 2026: the Ministry of Economy and Finance's 29 July 2026 'Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting' remains the latest official statement addressing the stock-market correction; no newer market-stabilization statement has been published.

Re-checked 10 August 2026: MOFE's press center lists no crisis-specific statement newer than the 29 July 2026 'Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting'; its most recent entries since are routine releases (July Consumer Price Index, the 2026 Tax Revision Bill, monthly industrial statistics, the August Treasury Bond Issuance Plan). The Bank of Korea's English press-release listing page returned a placeholder indicating content was being updated, and its main site showed only routine items (a balance-of-payments surplus report, foreign-reserves data) through 7 August 2026. No new emergency stabilization measure has been announced since the 29 July intervention (a 20% single-stock cap on leveraged ETF portfolios, higher trading costs, and a legal basis for further stabilization measures).

Re-checked 11 August 2026: the Ministry of Economy and Finance's press-release list shows no statement newer than the 29 July 2026 'Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting' addressing stock-market volatility or intervention; the list's most recent entries (Consumer Price Index, July 2026 - 4 August; 2026 Tax Revision Bill - 3 August; Monthly Industrial Statistics, June 2026 - 31 July) are routine and unrelated. The Bank of Korea's English press-release listing page again returned a "content is being prepared / page is currently being updated" placeholder. No new emergency stabilization measure has been announced since the 29 July intervention.

description: South Korea's KOSPI index, which had surged to an all-time high in June 2026, underwent a sharp and volatile correction through July driven by intensifying Chinese competition in the memory-chip industry and concerns over major US tech firms' AI-related funding needs; the market triggered repeated trading-halt circuit breakers, including on back-to-back sessions in late July. The Bank of Korea's 16 July 2026 policy statement acknowledged stock prices had "underwent a sizable correction amid heightened volatility," and on 29 July the government convened an Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting of the Deputy Prime Minister/Finance Minister, the Bank of Korea Governor, and financial regulators, which announced new curbs on single-stock leveraged products, a 24-hour market monitoring system, and a commitment to establish a legal basis for emergency market-stabilization measures. As of 5 August 2026, South Korea's Ministry of Economy and Finance has published no press release newer than the 29 July Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting readout addressing stock-market volatility or intervention; its most recent releases (30 July Treasury Bond Issuance Plan, 31 July Monthly Industrial Statistics, 4 August Consumer Price Index) are routine and do not reference the correction. No allowlisted source has declared the correction over. Re-checked 8 August 2026: the Ministry of Economy and Finance's press-release list still shows the 29 July 2026 'Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting' as the latest release addressing the market correction (subsequent releases, e.g. the 2026 Tax Revision Bill and July CPI, are routine and unrelated); the Bank of Korea's press-release page remained unrenderable today, and no newer market-stabilization statement was confirmed from either allowlisted source. Re-checked 9 August 2026: the Ministry of Economy and Finance's 29 July 2026 'Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting' remains the latest statement addressing the market correction; the Bank of Korea published minutes of its July monetary policy meeting on 5 August 2026 discussing rate-hike considerations, but no new market-stabilization intervention or index-decline figure has been published by either institution. Re-checked 10 August 2026: no new emergency intervention has been announced by MOFE or the Bank of Korea since the 29 July 2026 measures; both institutions' latest public items are routine releases. Re-checked 11 August 2026: the Ministry of Economy and Finance's press-release list still shows no statement newer than the 29 July 2026 Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting addressing stock-market volatility or intervention (its newest entries, the 4 August Consumer Price Index and 3 August 2026 Tax Revision Bill, are routine and unrelated); the Bank of Korea's English press-release listing page again returned a "content is being prepared / page is currently being updated" placeholder. No new emergency stabilization measure has been announced since the 29 July intervention. Re-checked 12 August 2026: no official statement from MOFE or the Bank of Korea postdates the 29 July 2026 Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting; the Bank of Korea's English press-center page remains the latest in its series with no crisis-specific statement, and the 29 July emergency measures remain the most recent official government/central-bank action on file. Re-checked 13 August 2026: MOFE's press-center list and the Bank of Korea's press-release list show no new crisis-specific release since the 29 July 2026 Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting; BOK's English press-release page remains in a maintenance placeholder state. No IMF statement on the correction has been published. No allowlisted source has declared the episode resolved. Re-checked 14 August 2026: MOFE's press-center list shows no crisis-specific release newer than the 29 July 2026 Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting; the Bank of Korea's press page remains a maintenance placeholder. Status unchanged. Re-checked 15 August 2026: the Ministry of Economy and Finance's press-center list shows no crisis-specific release newer than the 29 July 2026 Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting (subsequent items — the 2026 Tax Revision Bill, 3 August; a Deputy PM bilateral meeting, 12 August — are routine and unrelated); the Bank of Korea's English press-release listing page again failed to render. No new market-stabilization measure or resolution statement has been confirmed since 29 July. Re-checked 16 August 2026: no new emergency market action has been announced by BOK or MOFE since 29 July 2026, indicating the acute intervention phase has concluded; status downgraded to contained pending any renewed crisis-level statement.

impact.summary: The Bank of Korea's 16 July 2026 monetary policy statement said stock prices "underwent a sizable correction amid heightened volatility due to growing concerns over AI investment and large-scale net sales of domestic stocks by foreign investors," citing persistent financial stability risks. On 29 July 2026, South Korea's Ministry of Economy and Finance convened an Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting — chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister/Finance Minister and attended by the Bank of Korea Governor and the heads of the Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service — after the stock market's decline, led by semiconductor shares, triggered market-wide circuit breakers on consecutive trading sessions. The meeting's official readout announced new curbs on single-stock leveraged products (investment limits, higher transaction costs, mandatory simulated trading), a 24-hour market monitoring system, and a commitment to establish a legal basis for emergency market-stabilization measures; participants judged Korea's underlying economic fundamentals (exports, corporate earnings, current account surplus) remained solid.
